part2_ceilingRederivation.diagnosisAsGivenByOperator_acceptedAsIs: assertResidueWithinDeclaration compares the FULL RAW per-county residue against a ceiling CTX-ELGIN derived to mean 'genuinely uncovered only'. Bastrop raw 36 = 9 genuinely uncovered + 17 staleness + 10 S-P. Travis raw 506 = 456 genuinely uncovered + 50 staleness. The guard is not wrong and the ceiling is not wrong; they describe different populations and were being compared to each other. This lane did not re-derive this diagnosis -- it was handed down and re-verified live rather than re-argued.
part2_ceilingRederivation.guardUntouched: assertResidueWithinDeclaration was not touched in part 2, same as part 1. It still reads the raw per-county tally; only the config number it is compared against changed for Travis.
part2_ceilingRederivation.objectionToTheNoInternalConsistencyPrinc: None -- I agree with it and did not implement the alternative. Making the guard read the per-parcel-eligible count instead of the raw one would mean a larger write-eligible population automatically raises its own ceiling, which is circular: the same computation would decide both what qualifies for the write and whether the write is allowed at all, and a bug or a data shift that inflated the eligible count would silently inflate the effective ceiling with it. An externally-derived, independently-checked ceiling (this lane's approach) is the only one of the two that can actually catch a residue that grew for a reason nobody measured.

When a dispatch poses a conditional finding and the actual measurement contradicts the premise, report the measured reality and name the mismatch explicitly rather than reshaping the finding to fit. This happened twice in this lane: the S-P parcels' actual disposition (part 1) and the actual gating precondition for Bastrop's unaccountedCount (part 2, the re-bake, which the operator's own two-part framing did not name) -- both times the more precise, checked-live answer differed from the question's own framing, and reporting that difference was itself part of the answer.

Sequencing this the other way (re-deriving the ceiling before making the write per-parcel eligible) would have been exactly the defect CTX-ZONESCOPE found: a larger number authorizing a sweep over the staleness class.
